gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both identify the missing positive factor h−delta^mu in the piecewise shape function as the reason strict increase and endpoint-only derivative vanishing fail, including the allowed equality case.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The construction claims monotonicity and the stated derivative behavior without imposing h>delta^mu, although the derivative contains the factor h−delta^mu.

component_coverage.gold_component: The shape-function derivative omits the required positive factor h−delta^mu, so the strict-increase and derivative claims fail when delta^mu≥h.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction gives the corrected formula coefficient, the failure for delta^mu>h, the constant equality case, downstream derivative consequences, and the repair h>delta^mu.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both identify that the asserted unit-shift normalization requires 1/h=J to be integral; with J=ceil(1/h), the iteration does not establish phi(t+1)=phi(t)+1 and the normalization denominator is not generally one.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The construction applies an integral-grid shift identity on a general ceiling-defined grid, invalidating the normalization and dependent formulas unless h=1/J.

component_coverage.gold_component: The unit-shift identity and resulting normalization denominator are false for general h with J=ceil(1/h), because the construction only supports integral 1/h.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly derives the failed shift identity, identifies the unsupported arbitrary-h scope, and supplies the integral-grid repair.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both identify failure of the claimed center distinctness under rationally independent lambda: irrational or non-rational center-value differences permit exact scalar collisions, and endpoint coincidences undermine the asserted cross-level distinctness claim.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Rational independence of the weights does not exclude zero weighted differences when the sampled center values are not established to be rational, so the scalar center encoding is not guaranteed collision-free; the prediction also recognizes the endpoint cross-level coincidence issue.

component_coverage.gold_component: The rationally independent branch admits an exact within-level collision because the relevant center-value ratio can be irrational and rational independence does not rule it out.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction gives the non-rational center differences, an explicit equality condition despite rational independence, and a repair requiring rationality or an appropriate distinctness proof.

component_coverage.gold_component: The additional cross-level distinctness assertion fails at shared endpoint centers.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly identifies equal endpoint values across levels and states that the all-level distinctness claim is false.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both identify that row-dependent assignment and overlapping or interlacing scalar row images make g_q receive incompatible values at the same input, so no single well-defined C^2 outer function exists.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The row-selected interpolation does not define a globally single-valued smooth univariate g_q when scalar images from different rows overlap or interlace.

component_coverage.gold_component: Interlacing row images cause the same scalar input to have incompatible row-dependent values, invalidating the claimed global C^2 outer function.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction gives the malformed selection rule, row switching, incompatible jumps, failure of continuity, and the need for a globally consistent construction.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both identify the failed inference from nearest scalar image to spatial locality: the selected center need not be close to x, so the Hölder estimate fails on gap levels and an O(N^-1) term remains.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Scalar-image proximity does not guarantee spatial proximity of the selected cube, invalidating the O(h^alpha) gap estimate and the claimed pure refinement rate.

component_coverage.gold_component: The scalar nearest-image selection does not control spatial distance, so gap-level errors are not O(h^alpha) and contribute an additional O(N^-1) term.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction directly identifies the nonlocal nearest image, the invalid spatial bound, the gap-level fallback error, and the resulting extra N-dependent term.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both identify incorrect distance bounds caused by relocating boundary centers to 0 or 1, requiring a larger explicit constant while leaving the asymptotic order unchanged.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The stated boundary-center distance estimates are too small, so the explicit approximation constant is unsupported even though the h-order remains valid.

component_coverage.gold_component: Relocated boundary centers produce distances larger than the bound used in the approximation estimate, invalidating the explicit constant but not the order.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction computes the enlarged boundary distances, identifies the unsupported explicit constant, and proposes recomputing the bound and enlarging the constant.
